metadata.scenario: A prospect calls to dispute an unexpected setup fee that appeared on their first invoice. Category: Billing. Flags: billing_dispute. Customer type: prospect.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Robert Jackson. I’m calling about an unexpected setup fee on my first invoice. Hi Robert! I’m glad you called. I’m here to help. Can you tell me more about that fee? Yes, I noticed a $50 fee labeled as a setup charge. I wasn’t informed about this beforehand. I understand your concern. Let me check your account details quickly. One moment, please. Sure, take your time. I just want to know why this fee was added without prior notice. Thank you for your patience, Robert. I see that the setup fee covers the initial administrative work we do to coordinate your care. But I was under the impression that setup was included in the overall service costs. I completely understand where you’re coming from. We usually inform our clients about this fee during the onboarding process. I don’t recall being told about it. It feels a bit misleading. I apologize for any confusion. I can review your onboarding documentation to see if we missed something. That would be helpful. I would really appreciate a thorough explanation. Absolutely, I want to ensure everything is clear for you. Can I get your email to send the documentation? Sure, it’s robert.jackson@email.com. Thank you, Robert. I’ll send that over today. Would you like to discuss any other concerns while I have you? Actually, yes. My caregiver mentioned that I might need additional physical therapy sessions. We can certainly help with that. Our physical therapy services range from $110 to $140 per session. That sounds reasonable. I think I’d like to schedule a couple of sessions. Great! I can connect you with our physical therapist, Dr. James Rodriguez. Please do! I’d like to get started as soon as possible. I’ll set that up for you. Let me finalize the email regarding the fee and schedule your therapy sessions. Thank you, Margaret. I appreciate your help in sorting this out. You’re very welcome, Robert. I’ll follow up with you on both the invoice and the therapy schedule. Sounds good. I’ll be looking for that email. Thank you for your understanding. Have a great day, Robert! You too, bye! Goodbye!
